newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch shares end at new record as options expire.
newsitem.headline: Dutch shares end at new record as options expire.

text.p: Dutch shares on Friday continued in their bullish trend, ending at a record high for the fifth consecutive day.
The AEX index ended up 3.97 points at 608.88. Friday's trading also led to a new intraday peak of 611.48, set in the first half hour of an active early session.
The gains were the result of the expiring options contracts and the rush of short-covering that emerged as soon as trading began.
Some market makers had sold Nov 600 calls. Thursday's early Wall Street dip had hinted they would fall out of the money.
Subsequent New York gains and the positive start of European bourses on Friday left convinced the shorts that urgent buying was required, traders said.
"There was some panic buying going on (at the opening) as a dip below 600 looked impossible," one trader said.
Data showing U.S. October industrial production fell 0.5 percent, against a forecast rise of 0.2 percent, scuppered any hopes that the market might be led down by other exchanges.
Within the Netherlands, equities continued to be draw funds from the bond market and its unattractive yields.
"Bonds really offer very little," one trader said.
Few individual stocks stood out in a day of overall gain.
However, Aegon dipped 1.50 guilders to 93.30 after the release of third quarter figures. Its net profit of 1.10 billion guilders in the first nine months was in line with analysts expectations.
Traders said the fall of the share price was a reaction more to its steady gains this week than to the published results.
"It's gained about 3.50 (guilders) this week, so the loss today is not really significant," one trader said.
